Where to Buy Coveted Pre-Loved and Vintage Fashion Online

Keen for a low-slung belt à la Paris Hilton in the noughties?
Shopping WriterSangeeta Kocharekar
24 November, 2026
Make us your preferred source

Second-hand shopping used to mean giving up your Saturday to rummage through racks at thrift stores and weekend markets, hoping you’d find something special. These days, it can be as simple as opening your laptop, with a growing list of online stores selling pre-loved and vintage fashion.

Advertisement

Shopping online has its perks. You can search by brand, size, era and price, rather than flicking through hangers. You can also easily compare prices across several sellers, set alerts for the exact item you’re after, and shop from stores in Paris, Tokyo and New York without leaving the couch. Many luxury resale sites also authenticate designer pieces before they’re sold, which takes the risk out of buying a big-ticket item second-hand.

There’s a store for every kind of shopper. Luxury resale platforms specialise in authenticated designer bags, shoes and ready-to-wear. Peer-to-peer marketplaces let you buy directly from other people’s wardrobes, often at a fraction of the original price. Curated vintage boutiques, many of which started on Instagram, hand-pick pieces from specific eras or styles, so the hunting’s done for you.

So, if you’re looking for a rare Fendi Baguette, a low-slung belt à la Paris Hilton in the noughties, or something straight out of the swinging sixties, these are the best places to shop second-hand online in Australia.

Advertisement

marie claire Australia’s Top Picks For Online Vintage Stores:

  • Best overall online vintage store: Depop
  • Best Australian online vintage store: Trading In Style
  • Best international luxury online vintage store: Farfetch Pre-Owned
  • Best for rare pieces: eBay
  • Best online vintage store for designer bags: The RealReal

Depop

What sets Depop apart is its user-friendliness. The app is image-led and the feed is easy to scroll, view and shop. Depop’s algorithm will quickly learn the pieces you want to see as soon as you start ‘liking’ or searching the app. Selling is free and takes minutes, which means a constant stream of new listings at prices that are hard to beat. I’m an avid Depop buyer and seller, and my favourite find is a Mandarin-collar button-up top I scored for only $15. There is a treasure trove of high-quality items to buy, and I always feel secure with my payments and shipping, thanks to readable user reviews.

shop now At DEPOP

Blue Spinach

Blue Spinach was started by Jane Thompson as a secondhand store in Sydney’s Darlinghurst in 1996. It has since gone online-only, though it has an appointment-only showroom in Redfern, where you can request to view an item before you buy. Each listing has a handful of photos so you can really see the item before committing, and a team of expert authenticators examines every item before it’s sold. Items are graded by condition: good, very good, excellent and pristine.

shop now At BLUE SPINACH
Advertisement

Trading In Style

Luxury consignment store Trading In Style was founded by friends Jenna Isaacman and Bianca Picherit in 2018. If you happen to be in Sydney, you can visit the store in Randwick. Otherwise, almost everything is listed online, where helpful ‘edits’ include ‘Under $500’, ‘Under $1000’ and ‘Capsule Wardrobe’. Items are usually listed for about six weeks, so there’s constant turnover. Every piece is checked by the store’s in-house authenticators, then verified again by third-party services Entrupy and Luxury Authentication.

shop now At TRADING IN STYLE

Farfetch Pre-Owned

Farfetch launched Farfetch Second Life in May 2019, letting shoppers trade in pre-owned designer handbags for store credit. That has since expanded into a full pre-owned section, with clothes and accessories from brands like Chanel, Fendi and Bottega Veneta. I bought a pre-owned Gucci bag there last year, and was very happy with its condition, which showed only minor wear and tear. Keep an eye out, too, because many pre-loved items go on sale.

shop now At FARFETCH Pre-owned

The Pre Loved Closet (PLC)

The Pre Loved Closet (PLC) was founded in 2019 by Lisa Anderson, who initially started selling clothes that belonged to herself or her friends. Today, you can shop pieces from celebrity and influencer wardrobes, including those of Deborah Symond O’Neil and Erin Deering. There’s also a section online for edits, including ‘Desk to Drinks’, ‘The Investment Edit’ and ‘For the Bride’. If you’re in Sydney, you can view pieces at a showroom in Woollahra by appointment only.

shop now At THE PRE LOVED CLOSET

The RealReal

Founded in 2011 by e-commerce entrepreneur Julie Wainwright, The RealReal opened its first brick-and-mortar store in New York City’s SoHo in 2017. Today it has stores across the US, while its online store ships to around 60 countries. It’s best known for second-hand designer bags, but it sells clothes, watches and jewellery too. Expect fashion names like The Row, Ralph Lauren and Khaite. Like many other platforms on this list, it authenticates luxury items in-house before listing them. As it’s US-based, factor in international shipping and duties.

shop now At THE REALREAL
Advertisement

eBay

One of the biggest names in secondhand shopping, eBay was founded in San Jose, California, by tech entrepreneur Pierre Omidyar in 1995, and now owns Depop. With so much on offer, filters are your friend: narrow your search by brand, size, condition and price, and save searches so you’re alerted when something new is listed. Items are listed at fixed prices or, if the seller has opted for an auction, you can place a bid. For pricier pieces, check the seller’s feedback and ratings, look closely at the photos, and don’t be afraid to message the seller with questions before you buy.

shop now At EBAY

Vestiaire Collective

Vestiaire Collective was founded in Paris in 2009 by six co-founders. The team initially launched the platform with around 3,000 second-hand items sourced from family and friends. Today, it’s one of the biggest names in luxury resale, exclusively online. Like eBay and Depop, it’s a peer-to-peer marketplace, so you’re buying directly from other people’s wardrobes. When you check out, you can choose to have your item sent to one of its authentication hubs to be checked by experts before it’s shipped to you, or have it sent directly from the seller. In 2022, it banned fast-fashion brands.

shop now VESTIAIRE COLLECTIVE
